chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man whose wife divorced herself from him by Khul'a, is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before the waiting period of the woman who gave Khul'a has expired? He said: Yes, her bond of marriage has been severed from him and there is no reversion for him to her.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of reversion (taking the wife back without new contract)

ai.seo_question: Can a husband marry his Khul'a-divorced wife's sister before her waiting period ends?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in a Khul'a divorce, the husband's right of reversion (Ruj'ah) is extinguished, thereby allowing him to propose to the sister before her Iddah concludes. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of Khul'a compared to Talaq, where the husband retains the option to take back his wife during the waiting period. The hadith underscores the finality of the bond's dissolution from the husband's perspective, facilitating quicker remarriage arrangements.
